**Premise correction:** There is no per-user API rate-limiting middleware in this repository, so its registration location and request limits cannot be reported.

This codebase is [usememos/memos](https://github.com/usememos/memos). I searched exhaustively for rate-limiting concepts (`rate limit`, `RateLimit`, `limiter`, `throttle`, `429`, `TooManyRequests`, `quota`) across all `.go` files, as well as for any middleware/proxy config (nginx, Caddy, etc.) that might impose limits:

- The only hit for "rate limit" is a documentation comment in `internal/email/doc.go` (line 86: "Rate limit email sending to prevent abuse"), which is just prose advice about SMTP usage — it has no accompanying implementation and is unrelated to API request rate-limiting.
- The actual Connect-RPC middleware/interceptor chain, registered in `connect.WithInterceptors(...)` in `server/router/api/v1/v1.go` (lines 133-138), consists only of:

```133:138:server/router/api/v1/v1.go
connectInterceptors := connect.WithInterceptors(
    NewMetadataInterceptor(), // Convert HTTP headers to gRPC metadata first
    NewLoggingInterceptor(logStacktraces),
    NewRecoveryInterceptor(logStacktraces),
    NewAuthInterceptor(authorizer),
)
```

These interceptors (defined in `server/router/api/v1/connect_interceptors.go`) handle metadata propagation, logging, panic recovery, and authentication/authorization — none of them implement request throttling or per-user rate limits.

- No other middleware directory, reverse-proxy config (nginx/Caddy), or third-party rate-limiting library (e.g., `golang.org/x/time/rate`, `ulule/limiter`) appears in `go.mod`/`go.sum` or anywhere in the source tree.

So there is no per-user API rate-limiting middleware to point to in this repository as it currently stands.
